newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling sees 1996 sales at 1.7 billion yuan.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling sees 1996 sales at 1.7 billion yuan.

text.p: Jiangling Motors Corporation Ltd expects to post 1.7 billion yuan in sales in 1996, down from 1.96 billion last year, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Thursday.
This year Jiangling expected to sell 17,000 vehicles, mainly light trucks, against 20,500 in 1995, the newspaper quoted Jiangling's spokesman Xiong Zhongping as saying.
Xiong said that, despite the lower sales, Jiangling would report higher profits for 1996 thanks to lower production costs because of the higher domestic content of its products and better quality.

The domestic content ratio was raised by an average 10 percent this year, which resulted in higher profit margins, Xiong said. "The profit-to-sales ratio rose to 3.2 percent this year compared with only 0.5 percent in 1995," he added but gave no more details.
The same official earlier told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin Jiangling's net profits this year would be sharply higher than in 1995.
Ford Motor Co holds 20 percent of Jiangling's total share capital of 693.214 million shares.
